title: Kathua steel re-rolling & TMT: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A Kathua re-roller buys sponge iron, scrap and billet, melts and rolls it into TMT bars, and sells into J&K and Punjab Himachal construction demand. Cash is made on the spread between scrap/billet cost and rebar price, minus power and fuel. **The plant is a conversion machine: margin lives in the input-output spread and in how fast you turn inventory, not in the rolling mill itself.** Power is the second-largest cost after metal, so a unit with a captive furnace or a fixed-tariff PPA is a different credit from one buying grid power at spot.

Peer results show the sector can grow fast — Steel Exchange India at ~₹340 crore Q2 FY27 revenue, up ~45% YoY [5], and Rathi Steel above ₹200 crore, up over 30% YoY [6] — but those are South and North India players, not Kathua evidence.

## What has broken locally
The local data is the problem, not the sector. **J&K GST collections are -10.6% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%, and electricity demand is -0.5% against India +9.5% [D] — both point to weak local activity and weak local offtake.** Brent at $113/bbl [D] raises freight and power-linked costs for a unit already squeezed. The one positive is Hi-Tech Pipes starting commercial output at its Kathua plant in January 2026 [2], which confirms Kathua as a steel location but also adds a strong competitor for local rebar demand. The project-tracker listing [1] is a directory page, not confirmed capex — treat it as a lead, not a fact.

## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue the supplier, not the re-roller: dealers and fabricators selling into the Hi-Tech Pipes Kathua ecosystem [2], and job-work converters with a single anchor buyer.** Structure as invoice-discounted receivables from the anchor, with a 20-25% margin and monthly stock statements. Take every month: GST returns, power bills, stock-and-debtor statement, and a plant visit photo log.

## Early-warning signs
- GST filing gaps or falling e-way bills (monthly) -> stop fresh disbursement and inspect stock. - Power bill units down more than 20% month-on-month (monthly) -> ask for order book and shift pattern. - Rebar inventory days rising while sales flat (monthly) -> cut limit and demand debtor ageing. - Any rating downgrade or gearing above 1.80x, the level seen at Kubair Steel [9] (quarterly) -> review and seek additional collateral.
